subject: MSA addendum: ramp plan, pricing reconciliation and legal redlines
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@neptuneretail.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2024 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MSA addendum / ramp plan request

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward but need a clear path to scale from our current reserved pool to the higher burst profile we discussed. Procurement wants this captured as an MSA addendum (capacity ramp + pricing for burst tiers) and would like any SLA or data residency changes called out up front.

Attached is a simple CSV with our projected month-by-month token usage and a one-page note on timing. Key asks:
- Add 2x baseline reserved capacity in Q3 with burst up to 5x for 3 months.
- Price protection clause for the first 12 months.
- Audit log retention to be extended to 13 months.

Can you put together an MSA addendum draft or confirm your legal preferred process? Procurement needs a draft in 7 business days to make the July procurement window.

Cheers,
Liam
Procurement Lead
Neptune Retail
[Attachment: expected-usage.csv (csv)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@neptuneretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2024 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA addendum / ramp plan request

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file.

We're aligned on the timeline. Proposed next steps from our side:
1) I'll attach a mutual action plan and two capacity options (conservative and aggressive) for your review.
2) Please send any internal redlines (legal/ops) to us — we'll consolidate and route to our legal team.
3) We propose a one-week turnaround for internal review and then a countersign timeline to match your July procurement window.

Notes on your bullets:
- We can model a phased 2x baseline increase with a capped burst window; pricing for burst will be quoted as a blended CPM for that period.
- Price protection language is common; we'll propose language that ties increases to explicit triggers (e.g., new hardware pass-throughs).
- Audit log retention to 13 months is feasible but may need an export SLA for older logs; we'll call that out.

I've looped in Marissa (account lead) and Priyom (legal/business ops) to own the contract workstream. Attachments: mutual action plan, capacity options.

--
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Strategic 
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan.docx]
[Attachment: capacity_options.pdf]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@neptuneretail.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@neptuneretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2024 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA addendum / ramp plan request

Thanks Jasmine — attaching Neptune's first-pass redlines to the MSA addendum we discussed. Major redlines to flag:
- We replaced the proposed burst pricing with a fixed per-token surcharge cap rather than a blended CPM.
- Added a clause requiring 30 days' notice before any SLA changes that impact latency commitments.
- Requested audit log exports on a monthly basis for the first 6 months.

Redlines are high-level but should give you what legal needs to start. Our counsel (Elaine) is cc'd — she can explain the intent on the price cap language.

Attached: Neptune_MSA_Addendum_v1_redlines.pdf

Best,
Liam
[Attachment: Neptune_MSA_Addendum_v1_redlines.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2024 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Neptune redlines — legal review and high-risk flagging

Team — forwarding Neptune's redlines. Quick asks for legal ops:
- Priyom, can you do a redline review and produce a short "risk & ask" memo that: (a) lists any non-starters, (b) suggests alternative language for the fixed surcharge cap, and (c) highlights operational impacts for audit export cadence?
- Target: initial legal summary and proposed counter language by EOD 10 Jun so we can stay in the July procurement window.
- If anything needs an exec escalation (pricing concessions >20% of ARR run-rate or SLA change that affects uptime targets), flag it explicitly.

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, Jun 4, 2024 at 10:38 AM Liam O'Connor <liam@neptuneretail.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Jasmine — attaching Neptune's first-pass redlines to the MSA addendum we discussed. Major redlines to flag:
> > - We replaced the proposed burst pricing with a fixed per-token surcharge cap rather than a blended CPM.
> > - Added a clause requiring 30 days' notice before any SLA changes that impact latency commitments.
> > - Requested audit log exports on a monthly basis for the first 6 months.
> > Attached: Neptune_MSA_Addendum_v1_redlines.pdf

Marissa
Head of Sales, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@neptuneretail.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@neptuneretail.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2024 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Neptune redlines — legal review and high-risk flagging

Marissa / Priyom — thanks for moving quickly on this.

Priyom: if helpful, I'm attaching a short redline summary with the account POV (pricing sensitivity, procurement deadlines, and implementation timeline). After your memo we should sync for a 30-minute legal/finance alignment call before we share counters. Proposed slots: Thu 6/6 9-10am PT or Fri 6/7 11am-12pm PT.

Liam / Elaine — appreciate the prompt submission. We'll aim to return a clean countersigned path and proposed language by 10 Jun; if we need more runway we'll surface it immediately.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Strategic
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline-summary.md]
